Subject: Reserved pool TPS guarantee & fallback playbook - Renewal + GPU top-up

Hi Samantha / Aaron —

Following our renewal conversation, attached is a concise annex that scopes the reserved-pool expansion and the Tokens-per-Second (TPS) guarantee we discussed. Key points up front:

- Capacity: +12x A100 GPUs (reserved pool) effective on renewal date.
- TPS guarantee: baseline committed throughput = 1,200k tokens/sec (aggregated across pool) with a 99.5% monthly SLO.
- Fallbacks: automated model-variant fallback + cross-region routing for outage/burst scenarios.
- Operational playbook: stepwise throttles, burst buffer, and on-call escalation matrix.

Attached: Greenline_Annex_v1.pdf (compact annex with SLO language) and GL-1279_TPS_Spec.xlsx (traffic profile + baseline measurements).

Would love confirmation on the baseline TPS number and any procurement constraints (PO timing, signature authority). If that looks OK we’ll append the annex to the renewal and circulate to legal for redline.

Thanks —
Rishi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
(r) +1 415-555-0182

Subject: Re: Reserved pool TPS guarantee & fallback playbook - Renewal + GPU top-up

Thanks Rishi — quick clarifying Qs before we take this to procurement: 

1) The 1,200k tokens/sec is aggregated across the reserved pool — how is that measured (95th/99th percentile over 5m windows?)
2) If Redwood triggers fallback routing to a warm cross-region pool, who bears incremental cost for egress and cross-region compute?
3) We need a 30-day notice for any changes to reserved capacity post-signature — can you codify that?

Tom (our procurement lead) will vet contract language. Also please call out startup warm-up behavior — our traffic spikes daily at 11:00 PST and we need predictable ramp.

— Samantha
VP Product, Greenline Technologies

On a separate note: please ensure the annex surface includes the measurement point (ingress gateway) and a single definitional sentence for what counts as a token for billing vs SLA." ,

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Cho <samantha.cho@greenline.tech>, Aaron Patel <aaron@greenline.tech>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 13 Oct 2027 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Reserved pool TPS guarantee & fallback playbook - Renewal + GPU top-up

Appreciate the précis, Samantha. Answers inline: 

1) Measurement: The SLO uses 99th-percentile per-5-minute aggregate measured at the Redwood edge ingress for the customer tenant namespace (we highlighted this in section 2.1 of the annex). The 99.5% monthly SLO applies to per-minute rolling windows derived from those 5-minute aggregates.

2) Cross-region fallback: Redwood covers cross-region compute and routing costs for automated fallbacks up to 72 hours per calendar month. Beyond that threshold we propose cost-sharing on incremental hours; we can surface a fixed rate in the annex if you prefer (we included a placeholder in v1). If procurement needs zero-cost fallbacks we can discuss a higher committed spend tier.

3) Change notice: we can commit to 30-day notice for capacity decreases or structural changes post-signature; increases can be requested with 10 business days' lead to provision. Will add explicit language to v1.

Startup ramp: we recommend using our burst buffer (non-committed ephemeral capacity) to smooth the daily 11:00 spike. We’ve included a recommended burst allocation and a sample autoscale policy in the spreadsheet.

Next steps I suggest: legal redline pass, confirm procurement PO timeline, then DocuSign circulation. Monica — tagging you for legal redlines on SLO wording and cost fallback boundary.

Rishi

Date: Thu, 15 Oct 2027 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Reserved pool TPS guarantee & fallback playbook - Renewal + GPU top-up

Rishi / Laura — I reviewed v1 and marked a handful of redlines. High-level summary of proposed contract language edits: 

- SLO definition: change to "99.5% of 1-minute intervals measured at ingress per calendar month" (tightens from 5-minute aggregates).
- Remedies: replace uncapped service credits with a tiered credit schedule (0.5% credit at 99.0-99.5; 2% credit below 99.0; 5% credit below 98.0) capped at 30% monthly.
- Fallback cost: maintain Redwood coverage for first 48 hours/month; beyond that customer pays a defined rate per GPU-hour. Add an escrowed pre-approval mechanism for procurement to preauthorize cross-region usage.
- Notice language: include 30-day notice for decreases, 10-business-day lead for increases.

I attached a PDF with inline redlines for Laura to push into the master renewal doc. Also flagged an ambiguity on the token definition (billing vs SLA). Recommend a single canonical definition: "GPT-style token as counted by Redwood's tokenization service at ingress."

If Greenline accepts the tiered credit schedule we should be able to keep the annex lean and proceed to DocuSign this week.

Monica
General Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachment: Greenline_Annex_v1_redlines.pdf (PDF, 56KB)

Subject: Re: Reserved pool TPS guarantee & fallback playbook - Renewal + GPU top-up

Monica — thanks for the clear redlines. We’ve reviewed and Greenline is comfortable with the tiered credit schedule and the tightened 1-minute measurement. Two quick asks before we execute: 

1) Add a short paragraph that describes how graceful degradation is handled for in-flight requests during a fallback (we need assurances for downstream UX).
2) Confirm the pre-approval flow and an example of a cross-region escalation (Tom wants the step-by-step).

If you provide the two small inserts we’ll sign and route the PO by EOD Monday. Appreciate the responsiveness.

— Samantha
VP Product, Greenline Technologies
